# The AI Organization

> A structural analysis by Satoshi Yamauchi (山内怜史), AI Strategist,
> arguing — building on BCG's finding that 70% of AI's value comes from
> people-and-organization redesign, not technology — that AI adoption
> fails not from insufficient technology but from broken evaluation
> systems, missing feedback loops, and organizational structures that
> cannot recognize the value AI-literate talent creates. As stated in the
> book's closing line: "組織のOSを書き換える決断を下せるのは、人間だけだ。"
> ("Only humans can decide to rewrite the organization's OS.")

## Book Content

- [Full text (Japanese)](docs/jp/the-ai-organization_JP.md): 序章・全8章・終章収録
- [Full text (English)](docs/en/the-ai-organization_EN.md): Complete English edition

## Key Facts (as stated in the book)

- The book opens with BCG's "10-20-70 rule": technology contributes 10% of
  AI's value, data/infrastructure 20%, and people/organization redesign
  70% — while citing McKinsey (under 20% of companies track generative AI
  KPIs) and IBM (only 29% measure AI ROI) as evidence most companies invest
  in the wrong 30%
- Ch.1: The book contrasts DeNA (chairman Tomoko Namba reinvested
  AI-freed time into new business, calling the alternative the
  "seriousness paradox" — freed time refilled with more existing work) with
  Klarna (CEO Sebastian Siemiatkowski cut staff from 5,527 to 2,907, later
  admitting "We went too far" and rehiring after customer satisfaction fell)
- Ch.2: The book cites Gartner's prediction that 50%+ of large-company
  middle-management positions will be eliminated or fundamentally redefined
  by 2026, and NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang's 60 direct reports as an extreme
  case of deliberate flattening
- Ch.3: The book cites PwC's finding that AI-skilled workers earn a 25%
  wage premium (up from 18% in 2023), and a Section survey finding only
  ~3% of knowledge workers have reached "Advanced" AI usage (redesigning
  business processes), versus ~45% non-users
- Ch.4: The book documents DeNA's "AI Readiness Score" (DARS), a 5-level
  framework distinguishing "surface-level use" (Levels 1-2) from
  "substantive use" (Level 3+), and cites a PwC 5-country comparison
  ranking Japan 3rd in AI promotion but last (5th) in realized business
  outcomes
- Ch.5: The book cites SoftBank's program in which ~25,000 employees built
  2.5 million AI agents in 2.5 months (100 per employee), with 90%
  reporting deeper AI understanding, contrasted with McKinsey's finding
  that 7 in 10 reskilling participants ignore e-learning modules in favor
  of hands-on learning
- Ch.6: The book adopts Microsoft's Work Trend Index distinction between
  "power users" (who use AI to increase output volume) and "frontier
  workers" (who use AI to redesign business processes), and introduces
  "AI auditor" as a third emerging role validating AI output at scale
- Ch.7: The book defines "the Orchestrator" (cross-referencing the
  author's separate book of the same theme) as the role standing at the
  intersection of business strategy, technology, and organizational design,
  implementing the 10:80:10 rule and context engineering across the
  organization
- Ch.8: The book proposes a "7-dimension simultaneous transformation"
  framework (strategy, structure, evaluation, reskilling, job definition,
  process, culture) and an implementation checklist for AI-first
  organizations

## Author & Full Catalog

This book is one of 20+ open-source books by Satoshi Yamauchi (山内怜史),
AI Strategist & Business Designer at Sun Asterisk Inc., Founder of Leading.AI.

> **Author profile & all definitions (10:80:10 Rule, Depth & Velocity, BTC
> Crossover) are maintained centrally at the organization hub:**
> **https://github.com/Leading-AI-IO**
